Native units that transacted more than once are only counted once. L19: L20: | Name | MetricID | Unit | Interval | L21: | ----------------------------- | ------------ | ---- | -------- | L22: | Active Market Cap (1yr) (USD) | CapAct1yrUSD | USD | 1 year | L23: ### Details L24: * The state of the ledger is the one at the last available block for that day. L25: * Only the native units balance is considered, on-top tokens (e.g., ERC-20) are not included. L26: * Addresses owning 0 native units are not considered. L27: * For UTX-based protocols, last activity is the date of creation of the output. Mining reward outputs are not considered active. L28: * For account-based protocols, last activity is defined as either the time of the last debit of native units from this account, or the time at which it was created (if that creation wasn’t due to a genesis event or mining). L33: L34: ### Release History L35: L36: * Version 1.0 of CM Network Data Pro Daily Macro (End of Day) L37: ### Interpretation L38: L39: In contrast with Capitalization, realized, USD,this metric counts as valid on the fraction of supply which has moved in the prior 12 months. The intuition is to devise a measure of the economic significance of liquid and market-available supply, as evidenced by units that have made recent on-chain transactions. This metric can be volatile as large tranches of supply fall out of the eligibility window or as large sections move for the first time in over a year. Also referred to as free float network value or free float market capitalization. L141: * ETH Free Float Supply includes tokens on the Consensus Layer and Execution Layer L142: L143: ### Release History L144: L145: * Release Version: NDP-EOD 4.8 (Nov, 2020) L146: L147: ### See Also L148: L149: * Free Float Supply L150: L151: ### Availability for Assets L152: L153: {% embed url="" %} L154: L155: ## MVRV (Market Cap / Realized Market Cap) L156: ### Definition L157: L158: The ratio of the sum USD value of the current supply to the sum "realized" USD value of the current supply. L159: L160: | Name | MetricID | Unit | Interval | L161: | --------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------- | -------- | L162: | MVRV (Market Cap / Realized Market Cap) | CapMVRVCur | Dimensionless | 1 day | L163: L164: ### Details L165: L166: * Computed as CapMrktCurUSD / CapRealUSD L167: ### Chart L168: L169: L170: ### Asset-Specific Details L171: L172: * This metric is not available for assets that have full privacy, like Monero, Grin. L173: * For assets that have opt-in privacy features, like ZCash, it only takes the non-private balances into account, see Realized Cap’s entry for more details L174: L175: ### Release History L176: L177: * Conceptualized by [Adaptive Capital](https://medium.com/adaptivecapital/bitcoin-market-value-to-realized-value-mvrv-ratio-3ebc914dbaee) L178: * Released in the 1.0 release of NDP L179: ### Interpretation L180: L181: Market value to realized value (MVRV) has historically been one of the most reliable on-chain indicators of bitcoin market tops and bottoms. MVRV is calculated by dividing bitcoin’s market capitalization by its [realized capitalization](https://coinmetrics.io/realized-capitalization/). Realized capitalization can also be thought of as a gross approximation of bitcoin’s aggregate cost basis. L182: The intuition behind the creation of this ratio was to divide a price function by a ‘fundamental’ - Realized Capitalization. This gives you a ratio potentially indicating periods of overvaluation (when network value far exceeds its historical relationship to realized cap) and undervaluation. L183: Historically, a high ratio of market capitalization to realized capitalization has signaled that bitcoin price was near a local maximum, while a low ratio has indicated that price is near a local minimum. The few times that MVRV has dropped below one have historically been some of the best times to buy bitcoin. An increasing MVRV indicates that current sentiment is increasing fast relative to estimated aggregate cost basis, while decreasing MVRV signals the opposite. L220: ### See Also L221: L222: * MVRV (Market Cap / Realized Market Cap) L223: L224: ### Availability for Assets L225: L226: {% embed url="" %} L227: L228: ## MVRV Z-Score L229: ### Definition L230: L231: The ratio of the current market capitalization minus the realized market capitalization to the standard deviation of the current market capitalization. L232: L233: | Name | IMetricD | Unit | Interval | L234: | ------------ | -------- | ------------- | -------- | L235: | MVRV Z-Score | CapMVRVZ | Dimensionless | 1 day | L236: ### Details L237: * This metric is calculated as: (CapMrktCurUSD - CapRealUSD) / std(CapMrktCurUSD) L238: * MVRV Z-Score adjusts for the long-term volatility in market cap, making it easier to compare across different market cycles and identify extreme deviations from historical norms. L239: * Unlike regular MVRV (CapMVRVCur) or Free Float MVRV (CapMVRVFF), which are a raw ratio of market to realized value, MVRV Z-Score tells you how unusually high or low that relationship is compared to the asset's own historical behavior.
